title: The Truth About Factory Extended Warranties, Why You Want One And How Much I Paid
summary: An enthusiastic truck owner argues factory extended warranties are always worth it, covering pro-rated refunds, mileage-based pricing, nationwide price shopping, and resale value.

assertions.quote: before I'm even out of my factory warranty this gets crashed I get that money back

verdicts.note: True for many factory-backed plans as described, but refund terms vary by provider, and this isn't universal across all extended warranties, especially third-party contracts.

assertions.quote: if you wait till 10,000 Mi you're going to pay more money for it

verdicts.note: Plausible pricing mechanism tied to remaining risk at purchase, consistent with how several providers price these contracts, though pricing practices vary.

assertions.quote: you want to shop around and get the best price and you do that before you buy your vehicle
I promise you I will be able to sell that truck for $2,000 more than anybody that's selling one similar that does not have that

verdicts.note: Plausible that remaining transferable coverage adds some resale value, but a dollar-for-dollar premium equal to the warranty's cost is an anecdotal claim, not a verified market pattern.

assertions.quote: worth its weight in gold all day every day under every circumstance and condition and nobody will ever prove me otherwise

verdicts.note: Sweeping 'every circumstance' framing ignores cases like reliable, low-mileage vehicles where an extended warranty is poor value; this is promotional rather than evidence-based.

assertions.quote: you can also do it as a low interest or even a no interest payment plan on there for a year or two

verdicts.note: A commonly offered financing feature for factory service contracts, though terms vary by dealer and provider.
